Diagnosis
Left midshaft clavicular fracture
Date of injury 4th December 2022 5.
Plan
Refer for CT left clavicle.
Refer for physiotherapy.
For review after CT left clavicle has been done.
I reviewed Keith today in the company of his brother. He sustained a left midshaft clavicle fracture
on the 4th December 2026 which was managed nonoperatively. He use the collar and cuff for 6
weeks and last X-ray done January showed that the fracture was minimally displaced.
Today he is now at least 3 months following his left clavicle injury. He tells me that he continues to
experience pain around the fracture site and this pain also radiates to the mid aspect of the
clavicle.
He also complains that he has limitation of shoulder movement which he ascribes to the fracture.
I examined his left shoulder and I can palpate the fracture site which is mildly tender. He also has
some tenderness medial to the clavicle. He has some limitation of shoulder motion and abduction
is limited to 90° due to pain and also some extent of stiffness. She is neurovascularly intact in his
left upper limb. X-ray done today shows minimal increment in visible callus at the fracture site.
I reviewed this with Mr Patel today and the plan is for patient to have a CT of the left clavicle we
will review at his next visit. We will also be sending him for physiotherapy in order to improve his
left shoulder function. He can commence physiotherapy before he has the CT. I have relayed this
plan to the patient and he is happy with it.
Yours sincerely
Electronically signed
Dr Ijoukhumo Ethel Egbekun

clinician.summary: Male patient presented with left midshaft clavicular fracture sustained on 04/12/2022. Managed non-operatively with collar and cuff for 6 weeks. Now 3 months post-injury, still experiencing pain, limited shoulder movement and tenderness. Referred for CT left clavicle and physiotherapy

patient.summary: male patient has a fracture of the middle part of his collarbone. The fracture has not fully healed and is still causing him pain and difficulty moving his left shoulder. The doctor has recommended the patient have a CT scan of the collarbone and start physiotherapy to help improve the movement and strength of the shoulder. The patient will return for another appointment after the CT scan to discuss the results and next steps in his care

pharmacist.summary:
No medications were documented in the provided clinical letter. The letter focuses on the assessment and management of a left midshaft clavicular fracture. The key points are:

Left midshaft clavicular fracture sustained on 4/12/2022. Managed non-operatively with a collar and cuff for 6 weeks. X-ray in January showed minimal displacement. 
Patient continues to experience pain around the fracture site and limitation of shoulder movement 3 months post-injury. 
Examination findings include tenderness at the fracture site, limited shoulder abduction to 90 degrees, and minimal increase in callus on recent X-ray.
Plan is for CT scan of the left clavicle and referral to physiotherapy to improve shoulder function. Patient is to be reviewed after the CT scan.
No medications were mentioned in the letter.
